Okay, let me be your tourist guide ;-) I will concentrate on the
german locations, but one thing: Pere Lachaise is in Paris, which you
correctly place in the northeast of France - although for the French
it's the center I guess, the department (roughly equivalent to a
state, although the french constitution is not as federal as the
american) around Paris is actually called "Ile de France" - the island
of France, i.e. the heartland.

What references to Germany do we have? The infamous "Inbase Discothek,
Frankfurt" to me was always based on the once-famous 'Dorian Grey',
which is situated in Frankfurt Int'l Airport. The cradle of german
Techno music, although nowadays the real stuff comes from Berlin.
"Powerbase: Berlin" is pretty self-explanatory: Berlin is the capital
of the unified Germany (before that it was Bonn).
"Heidelburg Castle, Germany", as I pointed out in one of my last
Brujah newsletters, should actually be "Heidelberg Castle", but
nevertheless... The card artwork gives a good impression of how it
looks: A big old castle overlooking one of the most famous university
towns in Germany. It (the castle) is best known for being home of the
biggest wine casket in the world (I think, it's enormous and -
unfortunately - empty).
Ah yes, and the Chantry of Munich. Actually I have no clue what
specific sacred building the designers had in mind... The Frauenkirche
is the biggest church down here, but I wouldn't call it a Chantry. But
there are plenty of really beautiful Baroque cloisters and chapels
around here, so I guess it makes sense to have a Tremere guy taking
care of them being filled with some haunting music. Actually there is
a very obscure "vampirish" connection between Munich and a, well,
Chantry. Morris Pert, a scottish musician and composer, premiered one
of his orchestral pieces entitled 'The Ancient Kindred' (!) in Munich.
He released his albums on a label called Chantry Records... (Hehe,
good stuff for the next fiction part in my newsletter. Mark my words:
a giant conspiracy!)

A little bit OT, but one other word derived from German is the
often-misspelled "Rotschreck", which roughly translates to "fear of
the red", i.e. the dawn or fire.

Regards

Skaffen (entering Tourist Information: "Where is my bloody Chantry?")

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
Just a weird thought.

Unlike most CCG's, a lot of Jyhad/VTES is based on history and the real world
(in particular geographical locations, etc). On multiple occasions I've
wondered exactly where the location on this card is or exactly what it is and
in several cases I've even bothered to look it up!

Don't get me wrong. I'm actually quite educated. It's just that here in
America, we usually don't have that much of a focus on a lot of the more
notable European monuments and locations.

So I was thinking...wouldn't it be cool if one some Jyhad/VTES web-site, that
there might be a quick rundown (e.g. history lesson) on some of the locations?
I know it sounds a bit silly and it would probably require a great deal of
work, but maybe we'll learn more or something?

Interestingly enough, a few weeks ago I was watching TV and you'd be surprised
how often such subjects come up on History/TLC/PBS, etc. channels. I caught a
fascinating show on the Palace of Versailles (which I had known about before)
but I also found a neat episode on Pere Lachaise as well (which I previously
had no idea what it was). Apparently it's some famous cemetary in Northeast
France where lots of famous people (Chopin, Oscar Wilde, and Jim Morrison,
among others).

I've never been a geography buff and I still get a lot of the European cities
from Dark Sovereigns confused. Am I'm still wondering if "Inbase Discotek,
Frankfurt" is supposed to be some special place? And BTW, I know Ankara is the
capital of Turkey, but is there supposed to be some special Citadel or
something?

Just a weird thought.

Halcyan 2

Well, there are a few I can add:

Dartmoor, England - this is notable for being a large expanse of moorland. It
is a wild area, largely a protected nature reserve (national park deal). Famous
also for a series of murders that happened there in the 1960s.

Tomb of Rameses III -This is actually just north of Cairo, Egypt. The tomb is
sometimes referred to as the "Harpers Tomb" due to the two harpers playing to
the gods in four of the chambers. Rameses III is noted as one of the last Great
Pharoahs, fending off several major threats to the Egyptians during his
lifetime. He ruled Egypt for 31 years, dying at about 65 years old. Not bad for
a civilisation that didn't even have flushing toilets!

Inveraray, Scotland - We passed through there a couple of years ago whilst on
tour in Scotland. There is a Castle there, which is the home of the Duke and
Duchess of Argyll, the head of Clan Cambell. Legbiter might know more details -
Leggy?

London Evening Star - there is no such thing at the moment! There is an Evening
Standard, and a Daily Star, but no such thing as the Evening Star. However,
there is nothing to say that there wasn't years ago.

There are a couple that go without saying - Oxford university, England (one of
the most prestigious colleges in the land), Sacre Coure (Paris's 2nd most
famous Church after Notre Dame) etc etc.

Any ideas about Wasseschloss Anif, Austria anyone?

DH

There are many places in France, Switzerland or Belgium that are called Villars or Villers. It is a very common name for small cities or villages in the french (and spanish: "Villares") speaking area. Most of the times the full name is something like Villars-sur-Mere, which probably means "The village at the seaside".
Obviously V:tES is an english TCG, so all place names should be in English. But I doubt if there are alternative spellings for Villers or Villars in different languages, as none of the places is noteworthy enough (although quite a few have abbeys or ruins next to them...). On every map I look the town in question is spelled "Villers", even if the atlas gives mutliple spellings in different languages where needed (for example Liege - Luttich, Brussels - Bruxelles).

I guess we should leave it at that, Jeroens question was where the place is situated, and with LSJ's confirmation we now can be pretty sure that it's Villers (or Villars) in Brabant. And indeed Jyhad can be an educational experience, as I had to revive my rusty French to read through all these web pages.

Regards

Skaffen
